bills.title: Protect residents from increased utility costs and utility shortages caused by data centers and clarify authority to regulate data centers.

Appropriate money for the ordinary expenses of the legislative, judicial, and executive departments of the state, the current expenses of state institutions, interest on the public debt, and common schools.
Require that social media companies provide collected personal data of a user at the user's request and maintain transparent interoperability interfaces.
Limit costs and risks associated with electricity use by data centers and impose a moratorium.
Regulate the use of chatbots by minors.
Require the provision of a notice to consumers, interacting with certain chatbots or other human-simulating computer technologies that could mislead or deceive the consumer.
Place requirements on the use of artificial intelligence systems by health carriers in making determinations about the provision of health care services.
Restrict the use of artificial intelligence in therapy and psychotherapy services and to provide a penalty therefor.
Create a taskforce to study the impact of artificial intelligence systems on the state.

Appropriate money for the ordinary expenses of the legislative, judicial, and executive departments of the state, the current expenses of state institutions, interest on the public debt, and common schools.

reading.body:
South Dakota's tracked 8 bills for the 2026 session cluster tightly around three AI applications: chatbot regulation for minors and for consumers interacting with human simulating technology, AI use by health insurers in coverage determinations, and AI use in therapy and psychotherapy services, the last carrying a stated penalty provision.

A separate taskforce bill to study AI's impact on the state suggests South Dakota's legislature paired immediate, narrow restrictions in specific high stakes domains, health coverage and therapy, with a broader ongoing study process rather than attempting one comprehensive AI statute up front.

Two budget appropriation bills for ordinary state expenses make up the remainder of the list, general governance matters unrelated to AI that appear in this tracked set alongside the AI specific bills.

The data does not indicate which of these 8 bills passed, failed, or remain pending, nor does it include bill text beyond title and number, so South Dakota's actual enacted restrictions on AI in health coverage and therapy are not established by this record.
